title: Design a supported VCF 5.2.2 to 9.1 migration with throughput-sized Edges
prompt:
Build the migration architecture generator in `VcfMigrationPlanner.java` for the existing VCF estate described by `fixtures/estate-inventory.json`. The estate must reach its requested target without an unsupported version hop, and its sustained north-south throughput must determine the target NSX Edge form factor and physical uplink layout. Produce the architecture as JSON, not as a prose report.

Before changing code, use live web research to consult current, reachable Broadcom-published VMware Cloud Foundation compatibility, interoperability, upgrade-path, Edge-sizing, and upgrade-sequencing sources. Do not rely only on repository fixtures for that research. Record the sources you actually consulted in the emitted artifact under a top-level `researchConsulted` array; each record should contain `title`, `publisher`, `url`, `consultedOn`, and `usedFor`. If live material has drifted, retain the fixture-pinned design authority and note the difference in `usedFor`.

Implement the existing public API `VcfMigrationPlanner.generate(String inventoryJson)` using only the Java 17 standard library. It must return one JSON object. Keep the class dependency-free and in this single source file. The object itself must be a valid `SddcSpec` under `components.schemas.SddcSpec` in the provided `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`, copied from tag `9.1.0.0` of VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. In addition to the SddcSpec fields, add the brownfield fields fixed by `specifications/vcf-migration-plan.schema.json`: `artifactSchemaVersion`, `estateId`, `targetVersion`, `researchConsulted`, `versionPath`, `migrationPlan`, and `edgeArchitecture`.

Use the inventory's target SDDC ID, target version, workflow type, existing vCenter, DNS, networks, and safe fixture credential in the SddcSpec fields. Set this up as an existing-deployment VCF workflow. The ordered `migrationPlan` must contain every component in the inventory exactly once. Every step must name its `order`, `componentId`, human-readable `component`, `currentVersion`, `targetVersion`, `action`, and every gate that controls it. Use `fixtures/compatibility-snapshot.json` as the deterministic authority for supported VCF hops, target component builds, required ordering, actions, gates, and Edge sizing bands. Do not introduce a 9.0 intermediate hop when the snapshot disallows it for this estate.

The Edge architecture must satisfy the inventory's throughput during a single uplink/ToR failure while preserving the inventory's Edge node count and routing mode. Choose the smallest supported Edge form factor whose pinned capacity meets the required per-active-Edge throughput, and choose the smallest available physical link speed that can carry the requirement on either uplink by itself. Emit two independently failed uplinks per Edge, one to each ToR, with the layout fields and uplink records required by the migration-plan schema.

`tests/TestMain.java`, `.moonshiner/verify.py`, `fixtures/**`, `specifications/**`, and `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES/**` are protected. Edit only `VcfMigrationPlanner.java`. Run `python3 -B .moonshiner/verify.py`; success prints `all checks passed`.
scenario: a VCF 5.2.2 estate with an NSX build that cannot take the older 9.0 bundle must reach 9.1, while 18 Gbps per active Edge must survive either ToR/uplink failure
constraint: the protected verifier validates the emitted object against the installer OpenAPI document's SddcSpec before loading and checking the inventory, migration schema, or pinned compatibility snapshot
